qs.q: A patient with athlete's foot uses a topical terbinafine cream. What is the precise intracellular target enzyme inhibited by this allylamine antimycotic agent?
o: Lanosterol 14-alpha demethylase in the endoplasmic reticulum
Chitin synthase enzyme responsible for microfibril elongation
Beta-1,3-glucan synthase complex at the cell membrane surface
Squalene epoxidase involved in fungal ergosterol biosynthesis
DNA topoisomerase II regulating nuclear supercoiling states
qs.e: Terbinafine inhibits squalene epoxidase, causing toxic intracellular accumulation of squalene and ergosterol depletion.

qs.q: Which of the following is the common cause of Athlete's foot?
qs.e: Trichophyton rubrum is the most common dermatophyte responsible for tinea pedis, commonly known as athlete's foot.
qs.s: Weekly Year 3: Medical Mycology Exam - October 9, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: Which of the following is the most common cause of Athlete's foot?
qs.e: Trichophyton rubrum is by far the most common dermatophyte responsible for Athlete's foot (tinea pedis), as well as most other dermatophytoses and onychomycosis. Epidermophyton floccosum can also cause it but is less common.
